sub: Many English sayings are ancient — some come straight from Latin. Read the clues, trace them across languages, and separate the saying from its meaning.
kw: proverbs sayings latin carpe diem seize the day the apple doesn't fall far from the tree de tal palo tal astilla better late than never más vale tarde early bird etymology roots english spanish latin figurative language multilingual world languages high school grade 9 10 11 12

brief.label: Your mission
brief.h: Trace sayings to their meaning and their roots
brief.p: A proverb is a short, traditional saying that carries a lesson. Some English sayings even come from Latin. Find the meaning, compare it across languages, and notice where it came from.

win.p: You matched proverbs to their meanings, compared them across languages, and traced a Latin root — sophisticated work with figurative and traditional language.

clues.title: 'The apple doesn't fall far from the tree'
clues.body: This proverb means children resemble their parents. Spanish says 'de tal palo, tal astilla' (from such a stick, such a splinter) — a different picture, the same lesson.

clues.title: 'Better late than never'
clues.body: 'Better late than never' means doing something late is better than not at all. Spanish says 'más vale tarde que nunca' — an almost exact match, phrase for phrase.

clues.title: A Latin saying inside English
clues.body: 'Carpe diem' is a Latin phrase used in English that means 'seize the day' — make the most of now. Because Spanish also descends from Latin, it shares the root: Spanish 'día' (day) comes from Latin 'diem.'

clues.title: 'The early bird catches the worm'
clues.body: This means those who act early get the reward. Spanish has a vivid saying about the same idea of not being lazy: 'camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente' (a shrimp that falls asleep gets carried off by the current) — a completely different picture, a related lesson.

clues.title: Across time and languages
clues.body: Proverbs travel across time and languages. Some match closely ('better late than never' = 'más vale tarde que nunca'); some change the picture; and some, like 'carpe diem,' come straight from Latin — the ancestor of Spanish, French, and Italian.

clues.title: True, but off-topic
clues.body: One of the longest ancient scrolls ever found is over 40 meters long. That is a true history fact — but it has nothing to do with what these sayings mean.

locks.title: What does the Latin mean?
locks.q: What does the Latin phrase 'carpe diem' mean in English?
options: Seize the day — make the most of now
Rome was not built in a day
locks.reason: Clue 3 says 'carpe diem' means 'seize the day.' Recognizing a Latin phrase that lives inside English is a key skill for advanced readers and world-language students.

locks.title: What is true about these sayings?
locks.q: Check every statement that is TRUE (use the clues). Leave out the false one.

items.t: A proverb is a short, traditional saying that carries a lesson
English 'better late than never' and Spanish 'más vale tarde que nunca' match almost phrase for phrase
The Latin word 'diem' (in carpe diem) is the root of the Spanish word 'día'
Every English saying was invented in the last hundred years

locks.reason: The false statement is the trap: many sayings are ancient, and some come from Latin. The three true statements come straight from the clues.

locks.title: Build the meaning in order
locks.q: Tap the three lines in the ORDER that explains 'the early bird catches the worm.'

pads.e: 🐛 'So she gets the best chances first.'

locks.reason: The order builds the lesson: acting early, getting the first chances, and the proverb that names it. Proverbs compress a whole lesson into one line.

locks.title: Trace the Latin root
locks.q: The Latin 'diem' (in 'carpe diem') gave Spanish its word for 'day.' Type that Spanish word — or the English meaning 'day.'
locks.reason: Latin 'diem' → Spanish 'día' (English 'day' has the same meaning). Latin is the shared root that connects Spanish, French, and Italian — a central idea for world-language study.
